context.body: There happened to be there a wicked fellow, whose name was Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite; and he blew the trumpet, and said, “We have no portion in David,….
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Sheba calls Israel away from David, Judah stays, David confines the concubines, Amasa delays and is killed by Joab, and a wise woman negotiates Sheba’s death to spare Abel.
observations.label: Sheba’s rebellion exposes another fracture: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Sheba, David, Judah, Israel, concubines, Amasa, Joab, Abishai, and the wise woman, Jerusalem, Gibeon, and Abel Beth Maacah, rebelling, following, confining, delaying, killing, pursuing, negotiating, beheading, and returning visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Sheba’s rebellion exposes another fracture: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Sheba, David, Judah, Israel, concubines, Amasa, Joab, Abishai, and the wise woman · Jerusalem, Gibeon, and Abel Beth Maacah · rebelling, following, confining, delaying, killing, pursuing, negotiating, beheading, and returning · another rebellion ends through violence and local negotiation rather than restored unity
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 20:1–26

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 20:1–26 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places another rebellion ends through violence and local negotiation rather than restored unity inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Sheba’s rebellion exposes another fracture
